title: AsyncBEV: Cross-modal flow alignment in Asynchronous 3D Object Detection
claim: Under sensor time offsets a pretrained detector misplaces dynamic objects, while adding our module realigns predicted boxes with ground truth.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; concept diagram then baseline vs ours with zoom insets
description: Three panels. Panel a) is a rounded box with a concept diagram of asynchronous sensing. Camera icons sit above a gray arrow labeled 'data streams to detector', and LiDAR icons sit below it. Dotted orange and blue lines connect the sensors to the arrow. The timestamps t0 (blue) and t1 (orange) are marked, with Δt bracketed between them and a purple arrow marking the reference timestamp. Panels b) and c) show LiDAR bird's-eye-view point clouds with 3D boxes. Blue boxes are ground truth, green are true positives and red are false positives. Panel b) is the pretrained CMT, with boxes visibly offset from the ground truth and several red false positives. Panel c) is CMT+AsyncBEV (ours), with boxes that mostly overlap the ground truth. An orange rectangle in each of b) and c) marks a region, and an arrow links it to an enlarged inset. A legend sits in panel c).
caption: Multi-modal 3D object detection under sensor asynchrony. a) shows a general concept of asynchronous 3D object detection. b) shows multi-modal 3D object detection under sensor asynchrony of a pretrained CMT [ref]. Predictions exhibit large translation errors. c) shows our AsyncBEV improves CMT's robustness against sensor asynchrony and mostly corrects the spatial misalignment of predicted boxes.
abstract: In autonomous driving, multi-modal perception tasks like 3D object detection typically rely on well-synchronized sensors, both at training and inference. However, despite the use of hardware- or software-based synchronization algorithms, perfect synchrony is rarely guaranteed: Sensors may operate at different frequencies, and real-world factors such as network latency, hardware failures, or processing bottlenecks often introduce time offsets between sensors. Such asynchrony degrades perception performance, especially for dynamic objects. To address this challenge, we propose AsyncBEV, a trainable, lightweight and generic module to improve the robustness of 3D Bird's Eye View (BEV) object detection models against sensor asynchrony. Inspired by scene flow estimation, AsyncBEV predicts a dense 2D flow field directly from asynchronous multi-modal BEV features, taking into account the known time offset between these sensor measurements. The predicted feature flow is then used to warp and spatially align the feature maps, which we show can easily be integrated into different current BEV detector architectures (e.g., BEV grid-based and token-based). Extensive experiments demonstrate AsyncBEV improves robustness against both small and large asynchrony between LiDAR or camera sensors in both the token-based CMT and grid-based UniBEV, especially for dynamic objects. We significantly outperform the ego motion compensated CMT and UniBEV baselines, notably by $16.6$ % and $11.9$ % NDS on dynamic objects in the worst-case scenario of a $0.5 s$ time offset. Code is available at https://github.com/tudelft-iv/AsyncBEV.
